- When sentiment is 0.00 for 18+ days, model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >65.00), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >68.00) after a flat or declining period, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% for next 3–7 days.
- When sentiment history includes a single 0.25 (e.g., day 17), model often misreads momentum; treat as “potential breakout” and increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day window; apply a 2–5% upward bias to initial forecast days.
- If model forecast is >68.00 and true outcome is <65.00, apply a 5–10% downward correction to avoid overconfidence in high-price scenarios.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day windows with no sentiment signal; model often overreacts; apply 1–3% downward correction to forecast if price >67.00 and sentiment flat.
